policy: Mission status is a dated assertion from an official agency page. A capability or planned survey is FORECAST until a public observation or release is ingested with provenance.

sources.title: JWST Science Instruments and Observing Modes
sources.supports: Four instruments collectively cover approximately 0.6-28 micrometres.

sources.title: NIRSpec Instrumentation
sources.supports: NIRSpec covers 0.6-5.3 micrometres at resolving powers around 100, 1,000, and 2,700.

sources.title: NIRISS Instrumentation
sources.supports: NIRISS SOSS uses GR700XD over 0.6-2.8 micrometres at resolving power around 700.

sources.title: MIRI Medium Resolution Spectroscopy
sources.supports: MIRI MRS spans 4.9-27.9 micrometres at useful response, with resolving power varying from about 3,500 to 1,500.

sources.title: Habitable Worlds Observatory
sources.supports: HWO is a future flagship concept in architecture and technology maturation; engineering concepts are trade cases rather than a final design.

sources.title: ANDES instrument design
sources.supports: ANDES is a second-phase instrument with a 0.40-1.80 micrometre baseline and resolving power around 100,000.

sources.title: Plato
sources.supports: Launch is planned for March 2027; 26 cameras will study terrestrial transits and stellar oscillations.

sources.title: Plato factsheet
sources.supports: The spacecraft is in final testing and the science products are prospective.

sources.title: Gaia Data Release 3 contents summary
sources.supports: Gaia DR3 was publicly released on 13 June 2022 with astrometry, photometry, radial velocities, astrophysical parameters, variability, and non-single-star products.

sources.title: Gaia Data Release 4
sources.supports: The official DR4 page still describes the release as forthcoming; no DR4 rows are ingested.

sources.title: Roman Launch
sources.supports: Roman launched on 30 August 2026 and is travelling to Sun-Earth L2 before science operations.

sources.title: Galactic Bulge Time-Domain Survey technical overview
sources.supports: The planned survey uses 12.1-minute high-cadence observations over six seasons and is designed for microlensing demographics.
